subject: Biology
title: Ecological Pyramids: Numbers, Biomass, & Energy
topic: Eltonian Pyramids, Upright vs Inverted Models, Inverted Marine Biomass, & Inverted Tree Numbers
quickSummary: Ecological (Eltonian) Pyramids graphically depict trophic structures: (1) Pyramid of Numbers: Upright in grasslands/ponds; INVERTED in single tree ecosystems (1 tree T1 -> thousands of herbivorous insects T2 -> hyper-parasites T3). (2) Pyramid of Biomass: Upright in forests/grasslands; INVERTED in open oceans/seas because a small standing crop of rapidly turning-over phytoplankton T1 supports a larger biomass of zooplankton/fishes T2-T3. (3) Pyramid of Energy: ALWAYS UPRIGHT without exception in all natural ecosystems due to Lindeman's 10% law and the Second Law of Thermodynamics.

summaryBox.takeaway: Ecological pyramids illustrate trophic numbers, biomass, and energy. Number pyramids invert in single tree systems; biomass pyramids invert in open oceans; energy pyramids are ALWAYS upright without exception.

conceptBreakdown.content:
### 10.1 The Three Types of Eltonian Pyramids (Charles Elton, 1927)
- Ecological pyramids graphically portray the structural parameters of successive trophic levels ($T_1 \rightarrow T_2 \rightarrow T_3 \rightarrow T_4$) in an ecosystem.

### 10.2 Comprehensive Matrix of Ecological Pyramids

| Pyramid Type | Standard Orientation | Classic Inverted Exceptions | Biological / Ecological Cause |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Pyramid of Numbers** | **Upright** (Grassland, Pond) | **Inverted / Spindle-Shaped** in a **Single Tree Ecosystem** | A single large producer oak/tree ($T_1 = 1$) supports thousands of herbivorous insects ($T_2 = 1000$), which support birds ($T_3 = 50$) and thousands of ectoparasitic lice ($T_4 = 5000$) |
| **Pyramid of Biomass** | **Upright** (Forest, Savanna) | **INVERTED** in **Open Ocean / Sea Ecosystems** | The instantaneous standing crop of **Phytoplankton ($T_1 = 4\text{ g/m}^2$)** is very small, but their rapid turnover rate and high primary productivity support a much larger standing crop of **Zooplankton/Fishes ($T_2, T_3 = 12\text{ g/m}^2$)** |
| **Pyramid of Energy** | **ALWAYS UPRIGHT** | **NO EXCEPTIONS EVER** | At each trophic transfer, $\approx 90\%$ of energy is dissipated as metabolic heat ($R$). Energy reaching higher levels is strictly less than preceding levels (**Second Law of Thermodynamics**) |

### 10.3 Invariant Exam Diagnostic Rules
1. **Rule 1**: The base ($T_1$) always represents primary producers; the apex represents top carnivores.
2. **Rule 2**: If asked about an inverted energy pyramid, the answer is **IMPOSSIBLE IN NATURE**.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Spindle-Shaped Pyramids
conceptBreakdown.title: Spindle-Shaped Pyramids
conceptBreakdown.content: In a forest tree ecosystem where a single tree (T1 = 1) supports many herbivorous birds (T2 = 50) that are preyed upon by a single top hawk (T3 = 1), the pyramid of numbers is spindle-shaped (narrow at base and apex, wide in the middle).

conceptBreakdown.heading: Dry Weight vs Fresh Weight in Biomass Pyramids
conceptBreakdown.title: Dry Weight vs Fresh Weight in Biomass Pyramids
conceptBreakdown.content: Constructing biomass pyramids using fresh wet weight introduces significant artifacts because succulent plants (e.g., Opuntia) and jellyfish contain >95% water; drying to constant weight (dry biomass) provides true caloric accuracy.
